main_observation: PlainECGMAE remains near zero waveform prediction on both actual training batches and fixed train/validation diagnostic ECGs after 1000 updates.

additional_random_mask_two_ecg_check.caveat: Different training-mask policy only versus legacy fixed-mask tiny audit; does not establish generalization to unseen ECGs.
additional_random_mask_two_ecg_check.final_mask_repeats: 0..32; repeats 1..32 were encountered once during training

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Training-budget/optimization mismatch for diverse ECGs and masks
ranked_hypotheses.evidence: Only 6.4 mean ECG exposures in pilot; two-ECG fixed and changing-mask diagnostics succeed.
ranked_hypotheses.limitation: Tiny batch=2, constant LR and population=2 differ jointly from pilot batch=32, warmup/cosine and population=5000.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Time representation, embedding normalization, model/decoder capacity and topology influence learning efficiency
ranked_hypotheses.evidence: ST-MEM differs in all these components and exits near-zero prediction after 200 updates.
ranked_hypotheses.limitation: No component-isolated population-scale comparison is available.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Copied-layer initialization contributes to population-scale training
ranked_hypotheses.evidence: Legacy layers start identically; independent policy removes this.
ranked_hypotheses.limitation: Both policies reach nearly identical tiny-overfit loss; revised independent pilot is not yet available.

unsupported_explanations: Different ECG data or train/validation subsets caused the gap.
A broken gradient chain or universally zero parameter updates prevented learning.
The encoder became a constant vector for every ECG.
The original model failed because its decoder already reconstructed the task too easily.
ST-MEM is uniformly strong across every patch/mask setting.
recommended_controlled_checks: Fresh independent PlainECGMAE pilot at fixed patch/mask, followed by a longer matched run.
At a common batch/LR schedule, vary training subset size (32/256/5000) to separate data diversity from memorization.
Change fixed sinusoidal time encoding alone before testing embedding normalization or a larger model; preserve the global decoder/mask policy in the main research backbone.
limitation: No ST-MEM checkpoints or waveform NPZ were transferred by Git; current population comparison uses saved metrics, histories, gradients and feature statistics. ST-MEM has only seed 42.
